latin.559: §. XIV. SECULUM X, à Baronio in Annalibus atrô satis carbone notatum est, ob boni sterilitatem, ferreum, mali exundantis deformitatem, plumbeum, ob inopiam denique Scriptorum, obscurum nuncupatum, BELLARMINI etiam indignabundam hanc exclamationem promeritum: Vide Seculum infelix, in quo nulli Scriptores illustres, nulla Concilia, Pontifices parum solliciti de republica, subintellige Ecclesiastica;
latin.560: Habuit tamen etiam genuina de S. Cœna explicationis Professores & testes, ab Erigero Abbate Loviensi congestos, uti refert sæpè memoratus Cosinus Episcopus Anglus, ipsemet Anglorum suorum istius temporis Homilias, publice etiam in Ecclesiis Anglicis olim legi solitas, in medium adducens & ex Concionibus istis, p. 98. verba allegans, Bertrami assertis exacte parallela:
latin.561: Nam hunc in modum Homilia una, quæ Paschalis est, populum instituit: Multum interest inter corpus in quo passus est Christus, & corpus quod in hostia consecratur, corpus quidem in quo Christus passus est, ex Mariæ Virginis carne natum est, ac sanguine, ossibus, cute, nervis & membris humanis atque anima rationali constat; At SPIRITUALE ejus CORPUS, quod Hostiam appellamus, ex multis granis collectum est, sine sanguine, ossibus, membris, sine anima. Deinde Christi corpus quod semel mortuum est & à morte resurrexit, deinceps nunquam morietur, sed æternum est & impassibile, Hostia verò ista temporarie est corruptibilis in varias partes distributa, dentibus confecta & in ventrem transmissa, denique Mysterium hoc, pignus est & FIGURA; Christi corpus est veritas ipsa.
latin.562: Quod videtur, panis est; quod SPIRITUALITER intelligitur, Vita est.
latin.563: Altera verò Wulfini Episcopi Homilia, concisè equidem, at nervosè admodum sic informat: Hostia illa (scil. Sacramentalis) est Christi corpus, non CORPORALITER, sed SPIRITUALITER, non corpus in quo passus est Christus, sed corpus de quo locutus est, quando panem & vinum in hostiam consecravit.
latin.564: Hisce verbis tam veram & realem corporis Christi in S. Cena præsentiam, quàm unicum hujus præsentiæ genuinumque modum, à Christo Johan. VI. definitum, i. e. spiritualem, disertè inculcans. Quorsum etiam postrema Homiliæ hujus allegata verba interpretanda veniunt, ut nimirum non corporis Christi passi & crucifixi præsentiam realem, sed corporalem duntaxat, spirituali, in Homilia asserta, oppositam, in Cena S. inficientur.

pass_a.559: §. XIV. The TENTH AGE has been marked by Baronius in the Annals with coal black enough — called iron for sterility of the good, leaden for the deformity of overflowing evil, obscure finally for want of Writers — and has even earned this indignant exclamation of BELLARMINE: See an unhappy Age, in which no illustrious Writers, no Councils, Pontiffs little solicitous for the republic — understand Ecclesiastical;
pass_a.560: Yet it also had Professors and witnesses of a genuine explanation of the Sacred Supper, collected by Erigerus Abbot of Louvain, as the often-mentioned Cosin, English Bishop, reports — himself bringing into the midst Homilies of his English of that time, formerly accustomed to be read publicly even in English Churches, and alleging from those Sermons, p. 98, words exactly parallel to Bertram’s assertions:
pass_a.561: For in this manner one Homily, which is Paschal, instructs the people: There is much difference between the body in which Christ suffered and the body which is consecrated in the host; the body indeed in which Christ suffered was born from the flesh of the Virgin Mary and consists of blood, bones, skin, nerves and human members and a rational soul; But His SPIRITUAL BODY, which we call the Host, is collected from many grains, without blood, bones, members, without a soul. Further, Christ’s body which once died and rose from death will never afterward die, but is eternal and impassible; but that Host is temporally corruptible, distributed into various parts, finished by teeth and sent into the belly; finally this Mystery is a pledge and FIGURE; Christ’s body is the truth itself.
pass_a.562: What is seen is bread; what is understood SPIRITUALLY is Life. (Paschal Homily hinge after the FIGURE/truth contrast.)
pass_a.563: But another Homily of Bishop Wulfinus informs thus concisely indeed, yet very nervously: That Host (namely the Sacramental) is Christ’s body, not CORPORALLY but SPIRITUALLY — not the body in which Christ suffered, but the body of which He spoke when He consecrated bread and wine into the host.
pass_a.564: By these words distinctly inculcating both the true and real presence of Christ’s body in the Sacred Supper and the sole genuine mode of this presence defined by Christ in John 6 — i.e. the spiritual. To which end also the last alleged words of this Homily come to be interpreted, namely that they do not deny the real presence of Christ’s suffered and crucified body in the Sacred Supper, but only the corporal presence opposed to the spiritual asserted in the Homily.

559: §.XIV: Baronius marks the TENTH age with black coal — iron for sterility of good, leaden for overflowing evil, obscure for want of writers.
Bellarmine’s cry: unhappy age — no illustrious writers, no councils, pontiffs little solicitous for the ecclesiastical republic.
560: Yet it still had professors and witnesses of a genuine Supper explanation, collected by Erigerus of Louvain.
Cosin (English bishop) brings into the midst English homilies once read publicly in churches — words at p. 98 exactly parallel to Bertram.
561: Paschal Homily: much difference between the body in which Christ suffered and the body consecrated in the host.

The suffered body has Mary’s flesh, blood, bones, soul; the SPIRITUAL BODY we call Host is from many grains, without blood or soul — temporal, chewable; the Mystery is pledge and FIGURE; Christ’s body is the truth itself.
562: The Homily hinge: eyes meet bread.
Faith understanding meets Life — spiritual reading of the same host.
563: Bishop Wulfinus’s Homily, brief but sinewy: the sacramental Host is Christ’s body not CORPORALLY but SPIRITUALLY.
Not the body in which Christ suffered, but the body of which He spoke when He consecrated bread and wine into the host.
564: These words inculcate both true real presence in the Sacred Supper and the sole genuine mode Christ defined in John 6 — the spiritual.
The Homily’s close does not deny real presence of the suffered body — only corporal presence opposed to the spiritual. Stop before §.XV (Hildebrandine / Berengar).

563.gloss: not the body in which He suffered
